MX17 at LNL Legnaro · Geant4 feasibility · 8 Oct 2026

MX17 tests the ATOMKI ⁸Be claim at 3σ in ~16 days as built, and in ~1.2 days with big plastics

⁷Li(p,e⁺e⁻)⁸Be at the 18.15 MeV resonance, 1 µA. Geant4 of the full apparatus around a Li₂O target, with a selection that uses no Monte Carlo truth.

16–24 d

n_TOF hardware as built

3σ at R = 5.8×10⁻⁶, 1 µA (counting – template fit); 4–6 d on CN at 4 µA. Needs 3° MM segments or a 0.3 ns time-of-flight veto against cosmics.

1.2–1.6 d

four 75×75×5 cm plastics

The trigger_scint calorimeter option (~€90–140k). 7–10 h on CN at 4 µA.

3.3 % → 23 %

X17 pairs triggered

Both leptons reach the Micromegas in 39 % of decays; the two 20×30 cm plastics per arm are the bottleneck.

1

Details

Geant4 on the MX17_Full_Geant lnl branch (runs L1–L6, overnight 2026-10-08): X17 at four masses, Born IPC M1/E1 at 18.15, 17.64, 15.1 and 14.6 MeV, γ lines, one live day of cosmics, a chamber/backing scan, for the n_TOF stack as built and with four 75×75×5 cm plastics. Analysis: lnl/sim/lnl_geant.py; write-up lnl/FEASIBILITY_SIM.md; this deck reads lnl/out/geant/*.csv.

The days use counting in the best window (typically 130–165°) and an Asimov template fit over 90–180° with the IPC and γ₁ normalisations free (the M1/E1 mix fixed); with the mix also free the fit is ×2.3–3 slower. Rates and yields are lnl_rates.py.

2

Details

Arms going outward: air; Micromegas TPC (30 mm drift, 60 µm aluminised mylar window, active area 399.4 × 359.9 mm, faces at ±204 mm); SiPM scintillator wall; two 20 × 30 × 2 cm plastic bars; liquid scintillators. The real layout is a pinwheel, which the drawing leaves out; the toy acceptance uses plain planes at 204 mm.

Kinematics: the ⁸Be* recoils at β ≈ 0.006, which is negligible. The X17 edge (θ_min = 2·asin(m_X/E_X)) is 133.8–138.9° for m = 16.7–17.0 MeV at E_p = 1.03 MeV (out/kinematics.csv).

The beam is easy: both LNL Van de Graaffs cover the window

Energy range of the two machines against the ⁸Be resonances. Hover the bars and the lines.

Both machines cover it. 0.44–1.23 MeV is the whole programme: the two resonances and the off-resonance points ATOMKI and Hanoi used.

No neutrons below 1.88 MeV, so the current is limited by the target, not by radiation protection.

LNL already did this: the Marchi / Góngora-Servín spectrometer ran on AN2000 in 2023–24. Unpublished; they are the first people to talk to.

Access: the yearly LNL PAC (autumn). Contacts: A. Selva, pacbeams@lnl.infn.it.

Source: LNL beam sheet (2025 PAC call), CN paper arXiv:2605.12005. lnl/FACILITY.md

3

Details

From LNL's own beam sheet (lnl/refs/LNL_Beams_AN2000_CN.txt) and the 2026 CN paper (arXiv:2605.12005). Details, open questions and contacts are in lnl/FACILITY.md.

Ask LNL: energy spread and current stability at 1 µA for days on AN2000; whether CN can sit at ~1 MV for weeks and run overnight; floor plans of the AN2000 room and CN hall (the four-arm apparatus is ~1.5 m across); the next PAC deadline.

At 1.1 MeV, half the γ₀ is direct capture, not the resonance

⁷Li(p,γ₀)⁸Be cross section split into the two M1 resonances and a flat E1 direct capture. Hover the points.

total σ(γ₀), Zahnow 1995

M1 resonances

direct E1 capture

52 % of the γ₀ is direct E1 capture in ATOMKI's 2016 anomaly run (Li₂O 300 µg/cm² at 1.10 MeV); the 18.15 resonance makes the rest.

That matters: E1 IPC has ~2.5× the M1 rate at 140°, and ATOMKI 2022 sees its excess in direct capture too.

The 441 keV resonance is 50× stronger and makes 17.64 MeV pairs, where MEG II already limits X17. A thick target walks into it.

lnl/out/figures/excitation.csv (lnl_rates.py). Curves below 1 µb are drawn at 1 µb.

4

Details

Zahnow et al. 1995 (EXFOR A0639) S-factors for γ₀ and γ₀+γ₁, 98–1500 keV, converted to σ. The resonances are Breit–Wigner with constant widths (Tilley 2004); direct capture is the remainder. The split is not meaningful below ~500 keV, where the BW tail and the data disagree, but it is harmless at 1 MeV.

Checks against Tilley: σ(γ₀+γ₁) at 441 keV = 5.93 mb (5.9 ± 0.5); γ₀/(γ₀+γ₁) = 0.69 (0.69–0.72). MEG II's own 2026 normalisation is reproduced when their n and σ are used (factor 2 in the inputs, not the method).

X17 pairs open to ≥ 134°; the edge moves with E_p

θ_min = 2·asin(m_X/E_X) against E_p, for three masses. Hover the points.

m = 16.7 MeV

16.85

17.0

The X17 piles up above an edge at 134–139° at the 18.15 resonance; IPC falls steeply there.

The edge moves by ~10° over the scanned energies, so a real signal must follow it. That is the test the off-resonance points make.

The Geant4 reach uses the window that maximises S/√B (~130–165°) and a template fit over 90–180°; the edge sits inside both for all three masses.

Keep the film thin (≲ 300 µg/cm² ≈ 60 keV of energy loss): then < 1 % of the γ₀ is 17.64 MeV, and the signal sits at 18.15.

A beam that stops in Li metal at 1.10 MeV gets 77 % of its γ₀ from 441 keV. That is what happened to ATOMKI's 2016 targets (Sas 2022).

Use boron-free Li: ¹¹B(p,γ) puts 16–17 MeV γ in the window. LiF gives a free ¹⁹F E0 line (6.05 MeV) for calibration.

lnl/out/yields.csv (lnl_rates.yields_table)

6

Details

Thin-target yields from the Zahnow σ and PSTAR stopping (Li by Bragg subtraction), integrated through the film (lnl_rates.thin_yield). Recommendation (lnl/TARGETS.md): a few-hundred-nm film of LiF or Li₂O (or Li metal, or sputtered LiPON) on a 10–25 µm Al/C/Cu foil, in a thin carbon-fibre chamber. Heat at 1 µA is ~0.06 W in a 300 µg/cm² film.

Geometry is fine: both leptons reach the active Micromegas in 39 % of X17 decays (the toy said 45 %).

The trigger keeps 3.3 %. The two 20×30×2 cm plastics per arm cover a fraction of the Micromegas cone. Four 75×75×5 cm slabs keep 23 %.

Reading all 20 SiPM bars alone changes nothing (3.3 %): the plastics are the bottleneck.

Opening angle from the beam spot to the two MM centroids: σ68 = 5.3°.

lnl/out/geant/figures/geant_chain.csv, acceptance_geant.csv

7

Details

An arm is "ok" with a trigger leg (a SiPM bar AND a plastic, each ≥ 0.5 MIP) and a Micromegas segment whose charge centroid is in the active area. Pairs = the two ok arms with most scintillator energy. The arm choice matches the true lepton arms in 99.8 % of X17 events. The pre-Geant4 toy multiplied geometry by EPS_REST = 0.14 from the ILL; the real factor here is 0.084 as built.

The accepted X17 spreads from the 134° edge to 170°: the four-arm geometry favours back-to-back pairs, so only ~64 % of the tagged pairs fall in 125–155°. The template fit uses the rest.

lnl/out/geant/figures/geant_esum.csv

8

Details

The pre-Geant4 estimate assumed the n_TOF stack (~40 % containment) could not separate the γ₁ transitions (to the 3.0 MeV state, W ≈ 15 MeV, twice as frequent as γ₀) and counted their IPC in full. Geant4 says the LS make the difference: with them, nothing from 15.1 MeV reaches 13 MeV. The LS suffered pile-up at n_TOF; at LNL the rates are ~10³× lower, but whether they can be read is to be checked (ask). "As built, LS off": the window cannot exclude γ₁, and the reach goes from 15 to 19 days.

An upper E_sum edge: a muon through two arms leaves 20–35 MeV (with LS); an X17 pair has 17.1 MeV. ×20.

15° segments are not enough: the collinearity veto cannot see one straight track when each segment is 15° off.

3° segments or a 0.3 ns TOF (the lower arm fires 2.3 ns after the upper) bring them to ~1/day; together, 0.

lnl/out/geant/cosmics_*.csv

9

Details

Cosmic μ± from a 3×3 m plane, 1 /cm²/min, zenith perpendicular to the beam (sea level, no overburden). MEG II members showed in 2026 that cosmic two-arm coincidences make a ~140° bump in ATOMKI-type spectrometers; this is that effect quantified for MX17. Entries ≤ 2 are single events in one live day. The pointing cut keeps 90 % of X17 segments per arm (D = 135 mm at 15°, 57 mm at 3°; scattering in the window and gas sets the 3° value). σ_t = 0.3 ns per arm is an assumption (ask): at 1 ns the veto no longer separates the 2.3 ns muon delay. Two-arm cosmic triggers: 3.5/s as built, 22/s with big plastics; DREAM stays > 99 % live.

So the reach is set by the IPC statistics and by how well its angular shape is known (M1/E1 mix, interference).

10

Details

Per day = the ATOMKI 2016 anomaly, 1 µA rows of lnl/out/geant/reach_geant.csv. IPC = Born α × Geant4 acceptance × efficiency, weighted by the resonant/direct split of lnl_rates.py. EPC: 2×10⁸ γ of the four ⁸Be lines through the target, holder, chamber and dump: as built none passes in 125–155° (< 6×10⁻⁸ per γ); with the big plastics a few do (~4×10⁻⁸ per γ, ~10/day), < 1 % of the IPC.

11

Details

Counting: d = 9·B/S² in the window that maximises S/√B (130–165° typically). Template fit: Asimov over 90–180° in 2° bins, IPC and γ₁ normalisations free, M1/E1 mix fixed by the Zahnow decomposition; with the mix free too, ×2.3–3 longer (the accepted E1 IPC has its own 140–170° hump from the back-to-back geometry). All days divided by the DREAM live fraction (≥ 99 %). Signal counts the 18.15 resonance and direct capture with the same R.

Acceptance does not change. Keep the CFRP chamber and a low-Z backing.

EPC from the 8Be γ in the target, holder, chamber, dump: almost all at 25–92°: none in 125–155° as built (2×10⁸ γ), < 1 % of the IPC with big plastics.

Accidentals (2τ = 20 ns): ≲ 0.02/day. DREAM: 3.5 two-arm triggers/s as built, 22/s big plastics, all cosmics: > 99 % live.

⁷Li(p,p′) 478 keV never makes a leg. ²⁷Al(p,γ) 10.8 MeV (Al backing above 992 keV) and ¹⁹F lines (LiF): singles only; use Li₂O.

The 6.05 MeV E0 line is invisible to the n_TOF trigger (0 in 10⁶ pairs). Calibrate on 441 keV (17.64 MeV).

lnl/out/geant/material_scan.csv, epc_*.csv, daq_load.csv

12

Details

L5: X17 and M1 IPC with the chamber in Al 0.5 / 1.0 mm instead of CFRP 0.4 mm, and the backing in C 20 µm or Cu 25 µm instead of Al 10 µm, 5×10⁵ each. The resolution is the MM-centroid chord from the beam spot; multiple scattering in the chamber wall dominates. L3: γ lines from the spot (⁸Be 18.15/17.64/15.1/14.6, ¹⁹F 6.13/6.92/7.12, ⁷Li 0.478, ²⁸Si 10.76/1.78). L6: Born E0 pairs at 6.05 MeV.

A month reaches below the ATOMKI claim; with big plastics, ×5 below

The X17 ratio R on one log axis: ATOMKI's claim, MEG II's null, and MX17's 3σ reach after 30 days at 1 µA (Geant4). Hover the points.

The record is contradictory. ATOMKI (2016, 2022) and Hanoi (2024) see ~140° excesses; MEG II (2025) sees nothing; MEG II members (Sept 2026) show cosmics make a 140° bump in ATOMKI-type spectrometers.

What MX17 adds: tracks + timing that remove cosmics, and with big plastics ~9× ATOMKI's pair acceptance (as built, about equal: 3.3 % vs ~2.5 %). LNL's own 2023–24 data (unpublished) are the other result to wait for.

MX17 points: lnl/out/geant/reach_geant.csv (MM 15° + TOF).
